# Synthetic consultation: the imaginary paper-lantern workshop

## Who we are and the goal
This is fabricated test data for an imaginary workshop, not a real project or a reference product. The fictional team wants to compare three pretend lantern prototypes with invented units, artificial observations, and a repeatable rehearsal. None of these numbers describes a person, artist, commercial model, or real device.

## Measured facts (invented)
| Prototype | Imaginary cycles | Pretend latency | Status |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Amber kite | 17 | 23 ms | synthetic |
| Blue teapot | 29 | 31 ms | synthetic |
| Silver pebble | 43 | 47 ms | synthetic |

## What was tried and what happened
- Attempt one used cardboard gears and counted eleven imaginary pulses.
- Attempt two changed a fictional dial from three to five and recorded no real observation.
- Attempt three was a simulated rehearsal and has no relation to any existing work.

## Numbered questions
1. Which fictional prototype would be easiest to rehearse, and why?
2. What additional invented measurements would distinguish the alternatives?
3. How should the workshop present uncertainty without claiming real-world validation?

## How to answer
